title: Spatial transcriptome mapping identifies <i>Ppara-Anxa2</i> cross-talk in microplastic-induced hepatotoxicity
authors: Jung W, Abushukair H, Patil NY, Ampadu F, Firouzi M, Rus I, Choi J, Muthukrishnan SD, Shukla S, Tarantini S, Csiszar A, Mehla K, Kim D, Yoon JH, Kim D, Kim J, Jung J, Klementieva O, Shah YM, Yoshihara E, Singh PK, Joshi AD, Oh TG
biological_question: Does PE microplastic alter liver gene expression alone and on a MASH diet; which nuclear-receptor programme mediates it?
experimental_design: 2x2 factorial: diet (CD vs MASH diet) x daily oral gavage (vehicle vs PE), 8 weeks. Plus in-vitro 7-polymer viability screen.
species_strain_sex_age: Mouse, C57BL/6, MALE, 8 wk at start (Jackson)
biological_replicates_per_group: Phenotype n=5/group (Fig 1B) vs Methods 'n = 4 or 5'; bulk RNA-seq n per group NOT REPORTED in paper (GEO: 4/5/5/5); Xenium 19 samples on 2 slides, 'four to five biological replicates'; RT-qPCR 4-5
particle_size: 10-150 um nominal (Cospheric CPMS-0.96); measured distribution NOT REPORTED
characterisation_and_endotoxin: No DLS/SEM/zeta; no endotoxin test; unlabelled particles; non-plastic handling tools for spectroscopy only
dose: 2 mg per mouse per day (NOT body-weight normalised)
route_vehicle_duration: Oral gavage, daily, 8 wk, vehicle 0.1% Tween 20
diet_metabolic_stress_model: CD D09100304 (10 kcal% fat, sucrose-matched) vs MD D09100310 (40 kcal% fat, 20 kcal% fructose, 2% cholesterol)
groups_and_controls: CD+Veh, CD+PE, MD+Veh, MD+PE. No sham (non-gavaged) arm; no inert particle control
data_types: Bulk RNA-seq (NextSeq 2000, 2x150, target 15M reads); Xenium spatial (379-gene panel + 100 custom); H&E/NAS (blinded); serum ALT; hepatic TG; RT-qPCR; ChIP-qPCR; MTT
statistical_computational_methods: DESeq2 pairwise contrasts, |log2FC|>=0.38 & FDR<0.05; fgsea (min set size 1); one-way ANOVA + Tukey for phenotypes; beta regression / GLMM with mouse random effect for spatial cell proportions only
formal_interaction_tested: NO - no diet x PE interaction term anywhere; 'exacerbation'/'synergy' from pairwise contrasts and set subtraction
main_findings_and_directions: PE raised serum ALT on both diets and hepatic TG under MD; steatosis score up. PE DEGs: 503 CD-only, 182 MD-only, 97 shared. Shared PE-down: Fasn, Acly, Me1, Pnpla3; shared PE-up: Plin4, mt-Nd6, Cyb5a. Ppara and Nr1i3 induced vs CD+Veh. Spatial: midlobular hepatocytes up, Kupffer/stellate/lymphocytes down in MD+PE; Anxa2 up in central hepatocytes. PE-like particles detected in MD+PE liver by Raman/O-PTIR.
dir_lipid_lipogenesis: Lipogenic transcripts DOWN (Fasn, Acly, Me1) while histological steatosis and TG UP
dir_ppar_fao: Ppara UP (vs CD+Veh); Cyp4a12a up under CD. Cpt1a not reported
dir_cholesterol: Mixed: Hmgcr down under CD; Tm7sf2/Ldlr/Mylip listed for MD+PE (directions not stated)
dir_inflammation: Spatial inflammation niches up; lobular inflammation score only a trend; no Tnf/Il1b/Nlrp3 data
dir_mitochondria: Only mt-Nd6 up; no functional assay
dir_circadian: NOT MEASURED; time of sacrifice not reported
experimentally_validated: Partly. VALIDATED: qPCR (Anxa2), ChIP-qPCR (PPARa at Anxa2 peaks), in-vitro agonist/antagonist/siRNA. Ppara-null evidence is from EXTERNAL GSE8295 (different strain, no PE). No in-vivo PE x Ppara-loss experiment.
author_acknowledged_limitations: Segmentation spillover in liver Xenium; targeted panel does not capture whole transcriptome; study characterises mechanism rather than therapy
independent_methodological_concerns: Bulk RNA-seq n per group never stated; Fig 1B n=5 vs Methods 'n = 4 or 5'; cage = treatment group ('groups of mice housed together'); no interaction test; achieved depth/RIN/batch not reported; in-vitro screen not size- or surface-area-matched (55-5000 um at fixed 100 ug/mL); Raman run on already-used Xenium slides with no procedural blanks and only MD groups examined; ChIP-seq SRX runs come from a GPS2-knockout study - verify genotype; male only
accessions_as_stated: GSE294180 (own bulk); Zenodo 19603085 (Xenium); re-used: GSE245069, GSE282998, GSE8295, SRX5142528, SRX5028180
verified_data_availability: VERIFIED: GSE294180 public (19 samples, gene-level counts, SRA PRJNA1248512 19 runs). Zenodo 19603085 open CC-BY (h5 + cell metadata + UMAP). No code repository.
relevance_to_project: The team's source paper. Defines the design, thresholds and pairwise strategy being re-examined.

title: Polystyrene microplastics induce liver fibrosis and lipid deposition in mice through three hub genes revealed by the RNA-seq
authors: Li Q, Zhu K, Huang L, Niu X, Li L, Gao L, Xia Z
biological_question: Mechanism of liver fibrosis after chronic oral PS nano/microplastics of three sizes
experimental_design: 4 groups (H2O control, 80 nm, 0.5 um, 5 um), 12 weeks, single dose level. No diet factor
species_strain_sex_age: Mouse, ICR (outbred), MALE, 5 wk at start
biological_replicates_per_group: Allocated n=10/group; RNA-seq 'four independent biological replicate samples ... for each group' (=16); phenotypes n=5-8; qPCR n=5-6
particle_size: 80 nm, 0.5 um, 5 um nominal (Baseline ChromTech); measured size NOT REPORTED
characterisation_and_endotoxin: No DLS/zeta/SEM; no endotoxin; no surface chemistry
dose: 1 mg/L in drinking water (ingested mg/kg/day not reported)
route_vehicle_duration: Oral, ad libitum drinking water, 12 wk
diet_metabolic_stress_model: Standard diet only (composition/supplier not reported); NO metabolic-stress arm
groups_and_controls: H2O vs three particle sizes; no vehicle/surfactant control described
data_types: Bulk liver RNA-seq (BGI; platform/depth not reported); qPCR; western; IHC; H&E; Masson; Oil Red O; TEM; serum ALT/AST; oxidative-stress kits
statistical_computational_methods: limma for DE, |log2FC|>1 & adjusted p<0.05; DAVID enrichment; STRING+cytoHubba; phenotypes one-way ANOVA + uncorrected LSD post hoc
formal_interaction_tested: Not applicable (no second factor); sizes compared pairwise vs H2O only, no trend test
main_findings_and_directions: Liver weight and liver/body ratio DOWN; histological injury; fibrosis (Masson) up for 0.5 and 5 um; a-SMA protein up but mRNA unchanged; inflammation (Il6, Il1b, CD68) up; lipid deposition up; DEGs 333/602/758 for 80 nm/0.5 um/5 um; 87 shared DEGs; hub genes Acot3, Abcc3, Nr1i3, Fmo2
dir_lipid_lipogenesis: UP (Oil Red O, TEM; Fas, Scd1, Pparg, Apoc4 up by qPCR)
dir_ppar_fao: UP: Ppara up at all sizes; Acox1, Cpt1a, Mcad up (80 nm, 0.5 um)
dir_inflammation: UP, size-dependent (Il6, Il1b, Tnf, Cxcl2, CD68; IL-1b/IL-6 protein)
dir_oxidative_stress: NO CHANGE - 'GPX, MDA, and SOD were not increased ... of any of the three diameters'
dir_mitochondria: Not assayed; shared DEGs enriched for mitochondrial matrix (omics only)
experimentally_validated: Phenotypes, fibrosis, inflammation and lipid validated by histology/WB/IHC/qPCR. Hub genes validated at mRNA ONLY (qPCR); Fmo2 not significant; no functional test of causality
author_acknowledged_limitations: No limitations section; authors note hub-gene roles 'need further study' and that their oxidative-stress null is 'contrary to previous studies'
independent_methodological_concerns: limma described as 'for the microarray data' applied to RNA-seq - voom/trend unclear; quantification pipeline and depth unreported; whether each RNA-seq replicate is one mouse unstated; LSD post hoc has no multiplicity control; allocated n=10 but n=5-8 analysed with no exclusion criteria; several internal inconsistencies (oxidative assays described 'in ovaries' in male mice; 'all four RNA-seq datasets' for three contrasts); MeSH indexes strain as C57BL while text says ICR
verified_data_availability: VERIFIED: GSE245069 public, 16 liver samples (4 per group), supplementary matrix has raw read counts plus FPKM/TPM; SRA PRJNA1026899 16 runs. Fully reanalysable.
relevance_to_project: Non-MASH, different-polymer liver transcriptome with public counts - the most reusable independent comparison dataset found.

title: Polystyrene Nanoplastic Exposure Causes Reprogramming of Anti-Oxidative Genes Hmox1 and Sod3 by Inhibiting Nuclear Receptor RORγ in the Mouse Liver
authors: Ding P, Muniyappan M, Zhu C, Li C, Adam SY, Wang Y, Tyasi TL, Yuan P, Hu P, Liu H, Cai D
biological_question: Do PS nanoplastics repress Hmox1/Sod3 via nuclear receptor RORg and histone marks?
experimental_design: 2 groups (PBS vehicle vs PS-NPs), 28 days, single dose. No diet factor
species_strain_sex_age: Mouse, C57BL/6, MALE, 6 wk at purchase
biological_replicates_per_group: n=6 per group for phenotypes; RNA-seq libraries per group NOT REPORTED; ChIP-seq n/methods not reported
particle_size: 80 nm nominal (Baseline ChromTech); measured NOT REPORTED
characterisation_and_endotoxin: No DLS/zeta; no endotoxin; no dispersion protocol
dose: 1 mg per mouse per day (~40-50 mg/kg/day, not stated by authors)
route_vehicle_duration: Oral gavage daily, 28 d, vehicle PBS
diet_metabolic_stress_model: Standard chow only (composition in Table 1); NO metabolic-stress arm
groups_and_controls: Vehicle vs PS-NP; no dispersant control
data_types: Bulk liver RNA-seq (platform/depth/tool NOT REPORTED); ChIP-qPCR (RORg, P300, SRC1, Pol II, histone marks); ChIP-seq tracks without methods; qPCR; WB; H&E; CBC; serum ALT/AST/ALP; ROS/MDA/SOD/CAT/GSH kits; mitochondrial complexes; ATP
statistical_computational_methods: 'two-tailed non-parametric t tests' (test not named); DEGs |log2FC|>1 & RAW p<0.05, no FDR, DE tool not named; GSEA/Metascape/DAVID without thresholds
main_findings_and_directions: Body weight -10%, feed intake -8%, liver weight -19%; histological damage; caspase 3/7 +38%; ALT/AST/ALP up; SOD/CAT/GSH down, MDA +35%, ROS +46%; ATP and Complexes I/III/V down; 689 DEGs (389 up, 300 down); Hmox1 -45%, Sod3 -49%, RORg -19% (mRNA and protein); reduced RORg, P300, SRC1 and Pol II occupancy at Hmox1/Sod3; H3K9ac/H3K18ac down, H3K4me3/H3K27me3 up
dir_lipid_lipogenesis: Not measured directly; GSEA lipid-oxidation hallmark down (omics only)
dir_inflammation: Mixed: histological infiltration and WBC/monocytes UP, but GSEA inflammatory-response hallmark DOWN
dir_oxidative_stress: UP (ROS, MDA up; SOD/CAT/GSH activity down; Hmox1/Sod3 down)
experimentally_validated: Oxidative stress, mitochondria, histology, Hmox1/Sod3/RORg validated (kits, qPCR, WB, ChIP-qPCR). RORg CAUSALITY INFERRED - no knockout, knockdown, agonist or antagonist rescue
author_acknowledged_limitations: No limitations section; authors note discrepancies with other studies may stem from dose, size and route differences
independent_methodological_concerns: RNA-seq reporting essentially absent (no platform, depth, library n, DE tool); 689 DEGs at raw p<0.05 with no correction; ChIP-seq tracks shown with no methods or accession; body weight and feed intake both fell ~10%/8% with no pair-fed control (caloric-restriction confound); 'drinking water' in Discussion vs gavage in Methods; text vs table mismatches for WBC/monocytes; no sampling time reported
verified_data_availability: NOT AVAILABLE: PRJNA1305997 returns 'is not public' on NCBI (checked 2026-11-20); 0 SRA experiments linked. The only stated accession is inaccessible.
relevance_to_project: Chromatin-level mechanism absent from the team's dataset; a reminder to check circadian covariates. Data not reusable.

title: Oral exposure to polyethylene microplastics induces inflammatory and metabolic changes and promotes fibrosis in mouse liver
authors: Djouina M, Waxin C, Dubuquoy L, Launay D, Vignal C, Body-Malapel M
biological_question: Hepatic effects of sub-chronic dietary PE microplastics, and does PE worsen chemically induced fibrosis?
experimental_design: Exp 1: 4 groups (control, 36 um RB, 116 um GB, RB+GB), 6 or 9 weeks. Exp 2: CCl4 fibrosis model x PE (5 groups, 8 wk)
biological_replicates_per_group: Exp 1 n=10/group per time point; Exp 2 n=8/group
particle_size: Median 36 um (range 10-45) and 116 um (range 106-125), Cospheric; FTIR-confirmed pure PE (characterised in a previous paper)
characterisation_and_endotoxin: FTIR polymer confirmation; fluorescent (red/green) labelled; no endotoxin test; no dye-leaching control
dose: 100 ug per g of food (RB+GB group received 100 ug of EACH, i.e. double total mass); intake/mg-per-kg not measured
route_vehicle_duration: Dietary (spiked chow), ad libitum, 6 or 9 wk
diet_metabolic_stress_model: Standard food; NO high-fat/MASH arm. Second hit is CCl4 (0.2 ml/kg i.p.), not diet
groups_and_controls: Untreated control food; no inert-particle control
data_types: RT-qPCR ONLY (no RNA-seq); H&E; sirius red; Ki-67 and a-SMA IHC; TUNEL; liver cholesterol/TG/FFA; liver MDA; serum ALT/AST
statistical_computational_methods: Mann-Whitney U, p<0.05, mean+/-SEM; NO multiple-testing correction across a large qPCR panel; all comparisons pairwise vs control (and vs CCl4)
formal_interaction_tested: NO formal PE x CCl4 interaction; 'exacerbation' from pairwise contrast vs the CCl4 group
main_findings_and_directions: No mortality or body-weight change; AST/ALT up at 9 wk (36 um). Lipid genes: Cd36, Fabp1 up (RB+GB); Ppara ~2-fold up with both bead types; Acox1/Cpt1a/Acadm unchanged at 6 wk; Fasn, Acly, Acaca UP in all PE groups; liver cholesterol up (GB), TG up (RB+GB). Cyp2a4/Cyp2b10/Gsta1 up. Nrf2 battery up; MDA down at 6 wk but up at 9 wk. Inflammatory foci larger/more numerous; Il1b DOWN in single-bead groups. Ki-67 up, TUNEL unchanged. Pdgfa up; sirius red up. PE worsened CCl4 fibrosis (collagen, a-SMA, Col1a1, Vim).
dir_lipid_lipogenesis: UP - Fasn, Acly, Acaca up in all PE groups; TG and cholesterol up. OPPOSITE sign to Jung 2026
dir_ppar_fao: Ppara UP ~2-fold (same direction as Jung 2026) but downstream Acox1/Cpt1a/Acadm unchanged or down
dir_inflammation: UP overall but group-dependent (several Il1b/Il6 decreases in single-bead groups)
dir_oxidative_stress: ALTERED, time-dependent (Nrf2 battery up; MDA down at 6 wk, up at 9 wk)
dir_fibrosis: Weak in healthy liver; clear exacerbation on CCl4 background
experimentally_validated: All findings are targeted assays (qPCR, histology, IHC, biochemistry) - no omics. Fibrosis exacerbation validated by histology, IHC and qPCR but tested pairwise
author_acknowledged_limitations: 'it seems unlikely that PE MPs reached the liver in our experimental conditions. Therefore, the effects are more likely to be mediated indirectly' via gut dysbiosis/intestinal immunity; cannot tell whether particles were degraded by digestion; cross-study differences may be design or polymer
independent_methodological_concerns: FEMALE mice only (opposite sex to Jung 2026) and authors note Cyp2a4 is ~1000-fold female-biased; no multiplicity correction; CCl4 frequency stated as 'twice a week' (Methods) vs 'once a week' (Fig 7 legend); RB+GB received double particle mass so dose and combination are confounded; fluorescent dye with no unlabelled control; primer sequences 'available upon request' (not published); food intake not measured
verified_data_availability: No data accession; 'Data will be made available on request'. Not reusable.
relevance_to_project: The only other PE oral-exposure mouse liver study. Agrees with Jung on Ppara UP but reports lipogenic genes UP where Jung reports them DOWN, under different conditions. Argues PE effects are indirect/gut-mediated.

title: Polyethylene microplastics induced gut microbiota dysbiosis leading to liver injury via the TLR2/NF-κB/NLRP3 pathway in mice
authors: Xu R, Cao JW, Lv HL, Geng Y, Guo MY
journal: The Science of the total environment
biological_question: Does PE microplastic cause liver injury through gut microbiota disruption?
experimental_design: NOT VERIFIED (abstract only) - at least two concentrations plus control implied
data_types: Liver histology/function; fibril-related proteins; gut microbiota profiling; oxidative stress, inflammation, apoptosis assays. No transcriptome mentioned
main_findings_and_directions: Liver organ coefficient reduced; liver cell injury; fibril-related protein expression up and concentration-correlated; Desulfovibrio, Clostridia, Enterorhabdus, Bacteroides, Gemella up and Dubosiella down; oxidative stress, inflammation, apoptosis and necrosis induced; TLR2/NF-kB/NLRP3 activated in liver
experimentally_validated: NOT VERIFIED - from the abstract alone the gut-to-liver causal link is associative; no intervention (antibiotic, FMT, germ-free, knockout) is described
independent_methodological_concerns: ABSTRACT ONLY. Strain, sex, n, particle size, dose values, route, duration, statistics and data availability all unverifiable. Do not cite for numbers.
relevance_to_project: One of only two PE oral mouse liver studies; direction consistent with gut-mediated injury. Background only.

title: Single-cell transcriptome analysis of liver immune microenvironment changes induced by microplastics in mice with non-alcoholic fatty liver
authors: Liu W, Li M, Guo H, Wei S, Xu W, Yan Y, Shi Y, Xu Z, Chang K, Wei G, Zhao S
journal: The Science of the total environment
biological_question: How does microplastic exposure change the hepatic immune microenvironment in diet-induced NAFLD?
experimental_design: 2x2 stated in abstract: normal chow or HFD x water with/without MPs
biological_replicates_per_group: NOT VERIFIED - only total cells reported (43,480). Mice per group, the real statistical unit, not stated in abstract
polymer: Not named ('nano-scale' MPs; likely PS) - NOT VERIFIED
diet_metabolic_stress_model: Normal chow vs high-fat diet; formulation NOT VERIFIED
data_types: Single-cell RNA-seq of liver (43,480 cells); histology with NAFLD activity scoring; cell-cell communication analysis
formal_interaction_tested: NOT VERIFIED - abstract reports group comparisons only
main_findings_and_directions: HFD raised NAFLD activity scores; MP plus HFD further worsened steatosis, inflammatory infiltration and ballooning; MPs exacerbated pro-inflammatory response and affected hepatocyte stemness; Vsig4+ macrophages up and S100A6+ macrophages down; CD4+ recruitment up and CD8+ T-cell exhaustion up (vs control group)
dir_lipid_lipogenesis: Steatosis worse histologically; no gene-level direction
dir_inflammation: UP (immune infiltration, macrophage and T-cell shifts)
experimentally_validated: Histology validated per abstract; cell-population shifts are omics-only with no stated orthogonal validation
independent_methodological_concerns: ABSTRACT ONLY. Critically, mice per group is unknown - cell-level statistics across 43,480 cells from few animals would be pseudo-replication unless a sample-level model was used.
relevance_to_project: Closest published design to RQ2 in single-cell modality; supports the idea that bulk PE effects may partly reflect cell-composition change.

title: Oral Exposure to Polystyrene Microplastics of Mice on a Normal or High-Fat Diet and Intestinal and Metabolic Outcomes
authors: Okamura T, Hamaguchi M, Hasegawa Y, Hashimoto Y, Majima S, Senmaru T, Ushigome E, Nakanishi N, Asano M, Yamazaki M, Sasano R, Nakanishi Y, Seno H, Takano H, Fukui M
biological_question: Are PS microplastic effects larger under high-fat-diet-induced leaky gut than on a normal diet?
experimental_design: 2x2: diet (ND vs HFD) x MP (none vs PS), 4 weeks, pair-fed
species_strain_sex_age: Mouse, C57BL/6J, MALE, 7 wk at purchase; SINGLY HOUSED (1/cage)
biological_replicates_per_group: n=10/group; iPGTT and ITT n=5; 16S n=6; qPCR ambiguous (Methods 'six mice', Table 1 'n=10')
particle_size: 0.45-0.53 um nominal (Merck F-K1 050); measured distribution NOT REPORTED
characterisation_and_endotoxin: Dispersion stability in drinking water checked over 3 d (counts and intensity); no DLS/zeta; no endotoxin
dose: 1,000 ug/L in drinking water; per-mouse mg/kg/day not reported
route_vehicle_duration: Oral, drinking water, ad libitum, 4 wk
diet_metabolic_stress_model: ND = CLEA chow (4.6% kcal fat) vs HFD D12492 (60% kcal fat). NOTE: chow is not the matched purified control for D12492
data_types: NO transcriptomics. TaqMan RT-qPCR panels (jejunum and liver); 16S rRNA; GC-MS palmitate and SCFAs; histology (jejunum, liver H&E/Oil Red O/NAS); lamina propria flow cytometry; serum biochemistry; iPGTT/ITT/FITC-dextran; MODE-K cell experiments
statistical_computational_methods: One-way ANOVA + Holm-Sidak across four groups (JMP 13). No two-way ANOVA, no interaction term, no correction across outcome families
formal_interaction_tested: NO. 'MP effects only under HFD' rests on significance in one diet and non-significance in the other (difference-of-significance reasoning)
main_findings_and_directions: Hepatic Fasn 9.82x, Elovl6 4.28x, Scd1 3.03x, Tnfa 5.93x, Il6 5.51x, Il1b 6.17x (HFD+MP vs ND; all also significant vs HFD). NAS higher in HFD+MP; Oil Red O area up; hepatic palmitate up. Under ND the whole panel was null (0.86-1.22x). BUT iPGTT glucose was raised by MP under BOTH diets, and goblet cells/Muc2 thickness fell under both. Body weight unchanged; absolute liver weight LOWER in HFD+MP.
dir_lipid_lipogenesis: UP under HFD only (Fasn, Elovl6, Scd1)
dir_ppar_fao: NOT MEASURED (no FAO readout at all)
dir_cholesterol: Serum LDL-C higher in HFD+MP; no hepatic cholesterol genes
dir_inflammation: UP under HFD only (Tnfa, Il6, Il1b)
dir_fibrosis: Only as NAS sub-score; no dedicated stain
dir_circadian: NOT MEASURED; mice fasted overnight, sacrifice time not stated
experimentally_validated: qPCR, histology, flow cytometry, GC-MS all direct assays. In-vitro IL-22/Muc2 mechanism is cell-line only; no in-vivo IL-22 intervention
author_acknowledged_limitations: Did not measure plasma insulin in iPGTT; no dose-response or alternative size/concentration tested; ND trends 'not statistically significant in the present sample size'; FITC/GFP signal separation difficult
independent_methodological_concerns: 2x2 design analysed as one-way ANOVA; qPCR n ambiguous (6 vs 10); ITT dose 0.5 vs 0.75 U/kg between Methods and legend; ND chow vs purified HFD not matched; identical ND and ND+MP means/SDs reported for Scd1, Elovl6 and Fasn; pair-feeding to the lowest-intake group; GFP-labelled beads also used as tracer (dye-leaching); no data availability statement or accession of any kind
accessions_as_stated: NONE (no accession for 16S or any data)
verified_data_availability: No data availability statement found in the XML; no repository. Not reusable.
relevance_to_project: Closest published PS x HFD 2x2 with liver readouts and the clearest statement of the 'exacerbation' pattern - but qPCR only, and never tested as an interaction.

title: Long-Term Exposure to Polystyrene Microspheres and High-Fat Diet-Induced Obesity in Mice: Evaluating a Role for Microbiota Dysbiosis
authors: Zhai Z, Yang Y, Chen S, Wu Z
biological_question: Does chronic 5-um PS worsen HFD-induced obesity, and is the gut microbiota the mediator?
experimental_design: Three 24-mouse experiments: main 2x2 (diet x PS, 8 wk); the same 2x2 under antibiotic depletion; FMT into HFD recipients
species_strain_sex_age: Mouse, C57BL/6J, MALE, 6-8 wk; 3 mice/cage, 2 cages/group
biological_replicates_per_group: n=6 per group; 16S n=5; MASLD score n=5 (main) or n=4; Oil Red O n=4-5; immunofluorescence n=3; goblet cells reported as n=9 CRYPTS
particle_size: 5 um nominal but stated range 4.0-4.9 um (Macklin L815942)
characterisation_and_endotoxin: TEM morphology only; no DLS/zeta/FTIR; NO endotoxin test (notable as serum LPS is a primary outcome)
dose: 10 mg/L in drinking water; authors estimate 36 ug/day per mouse (~1.8 mg/kg/day)
route_vehicle_duration: Oral, drinking water, replaced every 2 d, 8 wk
diet_metabolic_stress_model: ND D12450B (10% kcal fat) vs HFD D12492 (60% kcal fat) - properly MATCHED purified control
groups_and_controls: ND, ND+PS, HFD, HFD+PS; plus ABX and FMT arms
data_types: NO transcriptomics and NO liver molecular work at all. Colon qPCR (Muc2, Tjp1) only; 16S rRNA; ELISAs (MUC2, LPS, cytokines); histology (liver H&E/Oil Red O/MASLD score, iWAT, colon); liver TC/TG; serum lipids; OGTT
statistical_computational_methods: One-way ANOVA + Tukey across groups; two-way repeated-measures ANOVA only for body weight over TIME (not diet x PS); Pearson (Methods) vs Spearman (Discussion) inconsistency; no correction over ~255 correlations
formal_interaction_tested: NO diet x PS interaction term anywhere
main_findings_and_directions: HFD+PS gained >17% more body weight than HFD despite eating less; liver weight, MASLD score, Oil Red O, liver TC and TG all higher; OGTT AUC and fasting glucose up; serum TC/LDL-C up but TG and HDL-C NULL. No PS effect on body weight under ND. Chao1 richness up under BOTH diets; Firmicutes:Bacteroidetes ratio DOWN (opposite to classic obesity). Colon barrier damage (goblet cells, Muc2, Tjp1, occludin down) under BOTH diets. ABX abolished the obesity and barrier effects; FMT from HFD+PS donors transferred weight gain, liver and adipose phenotype to HFD recipients.
dir_lipid_lipogenesis: Phenotypic only - liver TC/TG and Oil Red O up. NO lipogenic gene measured
dir_cholesterol: Liver and serum cholesterol UP; no genes
dir_inflammation: Serum LPS, TNF-a, IL-6, IL-1b, IL-17A up (vs ND); abolished by antibiotics; partly transferred by FMT (IL-6 ns, p=0.086)
experimentally_validated: Strong causal evidence for microbiota mediation via antibiotic depletion and faecal transfer - but no liver molecular data at all
author_acknowledged_limitations: Could not fully eradicate the microbiota; germ-free transfer would be more compelling; unexplained FMT glucose-AUC null; Gapdh reference-gene caveat; different particle sizes may have dissimilar effects; low vs high dose may differ
independent_methodological_concerns: 3 mice/cage with cage not modelled for a microbiota-driven phenotype; n inconsistencies across assays; goblet-cell 'n=9' is crypts not mice; serum cytokine contrast stated vs ND rather than vs HFD; in the antibiotic arm PS mice ate MORE but had LOWER glucose AUC (unexplained reversal); FMT donor feces pooled; no endotoxin test on particles
verified_data_availability: VERIFIED: PRJNA990701 exists, 20 SRA experiments, 16S amplicon of mouse feces. No liver data of any kind deposited (none generated).
relevance_to_project: Strongest causal evidence in the set that a plastic-plus-HFD liver phenotype can be microbiota-mediated rather than a direct hepatic particle effect. Disagrees with EHP 2023 on body/liver weight direction.

title: Obesogenic polystyrene microplastic exposures disrupt the gut-liver-adipose axis
authors: Zhao J, Adiele N, Gomes D, Malovichko M, Conklin DJ, Ekuban A, Luo J, Gripshover T, Watson WH, Banerjee M, Smith ML, Rouchka EC, Xu R, Zhang X, Gondim DD, Cave MC, O'Toole TE
journal: Toxicological sciences : an official journal of the Society of Toxicology
biological_question: Do drinking-water PS beads disrupt the gut-liver-adipose axis in chow-fed mice?
experimental_design: 3 groups (water, 0.5 um PS, 5 um PS), 13 weeks; plus a 4-week delphinidin sub-study
species_strain_sex_age: Mouse, C57BL/6, MALE, 12 wk at purchase
tissue: Liver; eWAT; PVAT; cecum; ileum; plasma
biological_replicates_per_group: '2 cages, n = 10 mice per treatment' (5/cage); liver mRNA-seq n=10; flow cytometry n=8-10; western n=4; adipose qPCR n=4-9
characterisation_and_endotoxin: No measured size/zeta/surface chemistry; no endotoxin; sonicated and renewed every other day
dose: 1.0 ug/mL in drinking water; intake estimated from 3-5 mL/day, not measured
diet_metabolic_stress_model: CHOW ONLY - no diet factor. Chow brand/composition not reported
groups_and_controls: Unsupplemented water control; allocation by CAGE (2 cages per group)
data_types: Liver bulk mRNA-seq (platform/depth/DE tool NOT reported); eWAT RNA-seq; adipose qPCR; bile acids by LC-MS; hepatic GSH/GSSG by HPLC; liver TG/cholesterol/FFA; histology; flow cytometry; plasma Luminex; DEXA
statistical_computational_methods: DEGs at q<0.05 with log2FC=0 (DE software NOT named); IPA pathways at unadjusted p<0.05; phenotypes ANOVA/Kruskal-Wallis with post hoc in Prism
formal_interaction_tested: Not applicable (no diet factor). Authors only speculate that an HFD 'second hit' might be needed
main_findings_and_directions: Liver DEGs: 283 (203 up, 80 down) for 0.5 um, 49 for 5 um; 5 shared. IPA: FXR/RXR and LXR/RXR for both sizes. Hepatic cholesterol UP for both sizes (p=.005 and .0006); liver:body weight DOWN. NULLS: liver histology unchanged, hepatic TG unchanged, ALT/AST unchanged, GSH/GSSG unchanged, ileum histology normal, plasma adipokines unchanged, beta-catenin unchanged. eWAT F4/80+ macrophages up with 0.5 um only. Bile acids size-dependently altered.
dir_lipid_lipogenesis: No steatosis; hepatic TG unchanged. Lipogenic genes not reported
dir_ppar_fao: Not reported for liver (PPAR signalling appears only as a delphinidin effect in adipose)
dir_cholesterol: UP - hepatic cholesterol increased by both sizes; FXR/RXR and LXR/RXR enriched
dir_inflammation: Liver histology clean, but Tnfaip3 and Ccl2 among top up DEGs; adipose macrophages up
dir_oxidative_stress: NULL - GSH, GSSG and GSH/GSSG unchanged despite NRF2/glutathione pathway enrichment (authors attribute enrichment to GSTs)
dir_fibrosis: Not assessed; Ctgf among top down DEGs at 5 um
experimentally_validated: Phenotypes, cholesterol, bile acids, flow cytometry validated. Liver DEGs are OMICS-ONLY - no qPCR confirmation reported
author_acknowledged_limitations: Did not determine particle distribution/accumulation in tissues; unknown whether PS disrupts redox balance or systemic inflammation; used pristine commercial beads rather than environmental mixtures; explicitly notes a high-fat diet could change the outcome; cross-study comparison difficult
independent_methodological_concerns: Cage-level allocation with 2 cages/group, cage never modelled; liver RNA-seq platform, depth, DE tool and batch never reported; IPA called at unadjusted p; whether n=10 libraries are per mouse unstated; delphinidin cohort lacks a PS-free + delphinidin arm; male only
verified_data_availability: VERIFIED but LIMITED: the Dryad record exists (CC0) and contains ONLY adipose delphinidin gene lists (2 xlsx + README, 386 KB). NO liver RNA-seq counts or reads are deposited anywhere. The liver transcriptome is not reanalysable.
relevance_to_project: Chow-only liver transcriptome with many reported NULLs - a useful counterweight to papers that report effects everywhere. Cage-confounded allocation mirrors the team's own concern.

title: Impact of the Oral Administration of Polystyrene Microplastics on Hepatic Lipid, Glucose, and Amino Acid Metabolism in C57BL/6Korl and C57BL/6-Lep<sup>em1hwl</sup>/Korl Mice
authors: Roh Y, Kim J, Song H, Seol A, Kim T, Park E, Park K, Lim S, Wang S, Jung Y, Kim H, Lim Y, Hwang D
biological_question: Do oral PS microplastics disrupt hepatic lipid, glucose and amino-acid metabolism differently in normal vs genetically obese (leptin-knockout) mice?
experimental_design: 2x2: genotype (WT vs Lep KO) x MP (vehicle vs PS), 9 weeks
species_strain_sex_age: Mouse, C57BL/6Korl WT and C57BL/6-Lep(em1hwl)/Korl, 7 wk at start; SEX NEVER REPORTED
biological_replicates_per_group: Allocated n=6/group; legends say 'five to six mice per group', each measured twice; serum lipid n not stated (values suggest very small n)
particle_size: 0.4-0.6 um nominal (Sigma); measured 607.23 +/- 8.27 nm, zeta -35.52 mV (possibly from a previous study)
characterisation_and_endotoxin: Size/zeta reported; fluorophore and surface chemistry not described; no endotoxin
dose: 100 ug/mL, 0.5 mL per administration (~50 ug), three times a week, 9 wk
diet_metabolic_stress_model: Standard chow for all; metabolic stress is GENETIC (leptin deficiency), not dietary
groups_and_controls: WT+vehicle, WT+MP, Lep KO+vehicle, Lep KO+MP
data_types: NO transcriptomics. RT-qPCR; western blot; ELISA; serum/hepatic biochemistry; H&E with NAFLD score; liver metabolites (HPLC/NMR, ambiguous); HepG2 and 3T3-L1 cells
statistical_computational_methods: Unpaired t-test and one-way ANOVA + Tukey (SPSS 27); legends mark '*' vs vehicle and '#' vs WT
formal_interaction_tested: NO - MP x genotype never tested; genotype-dependent claims rest on separate within-genotype pairwise tests
main_findings_and_directions: NULL body weight, liver weight, adipose weight, food and water intake. CONTRASTING by genotype: steatosis area and NAFLD score UP in WT+MP (604.6%) but lipid droplets/steatosis DOWN 26-49.8% in Lep KO+MP; PPARg and C/EBPa mRNA up 74%/72% in WT but down 22.7%/15.6% in Lep KO. SAME direction in both: FAS up, aP2 down, hepatic lipolysis proteins down, hepatic Glu up with serum Glu down, glycogenolysis genes up, GLUT4 and p-AMPK down, IR/IRS-1/PI3K/Akt up. Serum TC/TG/LDL up in WT only.
dir_lipid_lipogenesis: Genotype-dependent: steatosis and PPARg/C-EBPa UP in WT, DOWN in Lep KO; FAS up in both
dir_cholesterol: Serum TC and LDL up in WT only; hepatic cholesterol not measured
dir_inflammation: Only as NAFLD sub-score; no cytokines or macrophage markers
dir_oxidative_stress: Hepatic GSH among 7 changed metabolites (direction not stated); no ROS/MDA/SOD
dir_circadian: Not measured; sacrifice time not reported
experimentally_validated: qPCR, western, biochemistry and histology are direct assays; metabolite pathway mapping is computational
author_acknowledged_limitations: Did not measure MP distribution within hepatocytes/Kupffer cells/sinusoids; lacks MP kinetics (absorption, distribution, excretion); did not analyse inflammation, glucotoxicity or glucagon mechanisms; no direct comparison of diet-induced vs gene-deficient obesity models
independent_methodological_concerns: SEX of experimental mice never stated; effective n unclear and serum-lipid values suggest very small n; no interaction test despite a 2x2; dosing wording 'once daily (0.5 mL/day) three times a week' is internally ambiguous and the rationale quotes ug/L vs ug/mL; text vs Table 1 mismatch for LDL; abstract says serum metabolites while Results describe liver; Methods mix HPLC assays with Chenomx NMR analysis
verified_data_availability: 'available on request from the corresponding author'. Not reusable.
relevance_to_project: Shows that an MP effect can REVERSE sign depending on metabolic background (WT vs leptin-deficient) - directly relevant to RQ2 - yet the genotype dependence was never tested formally.

title: Chronic Nanoplastic Exposure Promotes the Development and Progression of Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease
authors: Han J, Jeong H, Lee C, Sung A, Choi YH, Jung Y
journal: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver
biological_question: Does chronic drinking-water nanoplastic exposure promote MASLD/MASH progression, and via hepatocyte SHH to stellate-cell Hedgehog signalling?
experimental_design: 2x2: diet (chow vs CDAHFD) x NPs (vehicle vs NPs), 12 weeks. UNBALANCED (6/12/6/12)
species_strain_sex_age: Mouse, C57BL/6, MALE, 7 wk at purchase
tissue: Liver; serum; isolated primary hepatocytes and stellate cells
biological_replicates_per_group: Allocated Chow+Veh 6, Chow+NPs 12, CDAHFD+Veh 6, CDAHFD+NPs 12; but every in-vivo legend says only 'n >= 3/group'
polymer: Polystyrene INFERRED from catalogue number only (Polysciences 17150-10); never stated in the text
particle_size: NOT REPORTED anywhere (no nominal or measured size, no DLS/zeta)
characterisation_and_endotoxin: Fluoresbrite-labelled; no endotoxin; no size characterisation at all
dose: 1 mg/L in drinking water; authors derive 0.18 ug/g body weight/day
route_vehicle_duration: Oral, drinking water, changed weekly, 12 wk
diet_metabolic_stress_model: Chow (M-diet) vs CDAHFD (A06071302, 60 kcal% fat, 0.1% methionine, choline-deficient) - a non-obesogenic steatohepatitis model
data_types: NO omics of any kind. Histology (H&E, Sirius Red, Oil Red O); IHC (caspase-3, a-SMA, GLI2, CD68); TUNEL; western blot; qRT-PCR; hepatic TG; hydroxyproline; ROS (DCF-DA); MDA; serum ALT/AST; in-vivo fluorescence imaging
statistical_computational_methods: One-way ANOVA + Tukey; all asterisks referenced to Chow+Veh; no exact p-values, effect sizes or CIs reported
formal_interaction_tested: NO interaction term despite the 2x2; several claims use qualitative wording ('seem to be higher')
main_findings_and_directions: Chow+NPs mice essentially unaffected ('normal liver morphology'). NPs did NOT change ALT, AST or liver/body weight. On CDAHFD, NPs increased hepatic TG, CD36 protein, ROS and MDA, apoptosis (caspase-3, TUNEL), Tnf-a/Il-6/Cxcl1/Cxcl2, CD68+ macrophages, fibrosis (Col1a1, a-Sma, TGF-b1, VIMENTIN, hydroxyproline, Sirius Red) and Hedgehog components (Shh, Smo, Gli2). SHH-neutralising antibody attenuated stellate-cell activation in conditioned-medium experiments.
dir_lipid_lipogenesis: UP via UPTAKE (CD36) rather than lipogenesis; hepatic TG up. Fasn/Srebf1/Pparg not measured
dir_inflammation: UP on CDAHFD background (Tnf-a, Il-6, Cxcl1, Cxcl2, CD68)
dir_oxidative_stress: UP (hepatic ROS and MDA highest in CDAHFD+NPs)
experimentally_validated: Extensive orthogonal validation (histology, IHC, WB, qPCR, hydroxyproline). Causal step is an SHH-neutralising antibody in vitro; no in-vivo Hedgehog blockade or knockout
author_acknowledged_limitations: Mechanism upstream of CD36 unknown; direction of causality for hepatic accumulation unresolved ('whether plastic particles induce liver disease or if the damaged liver cannot properly remove plastic particles'); human relevance limited by detection methods; NPs 'rarely had apparent pathophysiological effects' on a normal diet
independent_methodological_concerns: Polymer and particle size never stated - a basic reporting gap; unbalanced 2x2 analysed by one-way ANOVA with all contrasts vs Chow+Veh; allocation n (6/12/6/12) vs legends 'n >= 3'; drinking water is a cage-level exposure but cage structure not reported; chow vs CDAHFD not ingredient-matched; blinding not reported; westerns from 'representative mice'
verified_data_availability: 'available in the Supporting Information'. No repository. Not reusable.
relevance_to_project: Closest 2x2 plastic x diet design to the team's, and the clearest example of the inferential gap: an unbalanced 2x2 analysed as one-way ANOVA with every contrast referenced to the double-control group.

title: Polystyrene Nanoplastics Exacerbate HFD-induced MASLD by Reducing Cathepsin Activity and Triggering Large Vacuole Formation via Impaired Lysosomal Acidification
authors: Ahn J, Ryu K, Kim H, Seo HW, Jang M, Kim SH, Park Y, Son MJ, Lee HJ, Kwon OS, Chung KS
biological_question: Do oral PS nanoplastics aggravate HFD-induced MASLD by blocking lysosomal/autophagic function?
experimental_design: 2x2: diet (control diet vs HFD) x PS-NPs, at 8 and 20 weeks
species_strain_sex_age: Mouse, C57BL/6J, MALE, dosing from ~4 wk of age; INDIVIDUALLY HOUSED
tissue: Liver; serum; HepaRG and other human cell lines
biological_replicates_per_group: n=6 per group per duration; RNA-seq n per group NEVER REPORTED
particle_size: 50 nm nominal (Polysciences); measured size/zeta NOT REPORTED
characterisation_and_endotoxin: No DLS/zeta/TEM sizing; no endotoxin; GFP/Yellow-Green conjugated particles used for imaging not separately characterised
dose: 0.5 mg per mouse per day in an agarose jelly cube (NOT body-weight normalised)
route_vehicle_duration: Oral, voluntary jelly cube, daily, 8 or 20 wk
diet_metabolic_stress_model: Control = Teklad 2018S chow; HFD = D12451 (45 kcal% fat). Not ingredient-matched
groups_and_controls: CD, CD+PS-NPs, HFD, HFD+PS-NPs; vehicle = identical jelly cube without particles (well-matched)
data_types: Bulk liver RNA-seq (vendor ebiogen; platform/depth in an unread table); qRT-PCR; western; immunofluorescence; flow cytometry; H&E; Oil Red O; Picro-Sirius Red; serum ALT/AST/CHO/TG; cathepsin B activity; CYP3A4 activity; lysosomal imaging
statistical_computational_methods: DEGs at RAW p<0.05 and |log2FC|>0.5, DE tool NOT named; BH correction only at the enrichment step (ClusterProfiler); phenotypes one-way ANOVA + Tukey, 'comparisons are with the CD group'
formal_interaction_tested: NO. Transcriptome run as three separate pairwise contrasts with NO HFD vs CD contrast at all, so diet and particle effects cannot be compared
main_findings_and_directions: At 20 wk HFD+PS-NPs had higher body weight, liver weight, serum ALT/AST/cholesterol (serum TG unchanged), more diffuse steatosis. At 8 wk only body weight changed. DEGs: 361 (CD+PS-NPs vs CD), 628 (HFD+PS-NPs vs HFD), 1501 (HFD+PS-NPs vs CD+PS-NPs); 16 shared. Enriched: PPAR signalling, lipid metabolism, cell adhesion, actin organisation. In HepaRG: PPARG, CD36, PLIN2, PGC-1A, C/EBPA up, FABP1 down, HNF4A/ALB down, CYP3A4 up; mature cathepsin D down, cathepsin B activity down >80%; p62 and LC3-II accumulate; mTORC1 activity up; rapamycin rescued.
dir_lipid_lipogenesis: UP (PPARG, CD36, PLIN2 in human cells; lipid-metabolism KEGG terms in liver)
dir_ppar_fao: PPAR signalling enriched but it is PPARgamma that is measured and UP; PPARalpha never reported despite the antibody being listed
dir_cholesterol: Serum cholesterol UP; hepatic cholesterol genes not reported
dir_inflammation: UP on BOTH diets (F4/80 macrophages and MPO neutrophils increased even on control diet)
dir_oxidative_stress: Weak - only HO-1 up in HepaRG; no in-vivo ROS/MDA/SOD/GSH/Nrf2
dir_fibrosis: CONTRADICTORY - collagen deposition UP by Picro-Sirius Red but 'fibrosis-related genes were not significantly altered'
experimentally_validated: Mechanism validated in vitro by pharmacological rescue (rapamycin) and flux assays; in vivo the data are histology/serum only. Mechanism shown only in HepaRG - explicitly absent in HepG2, SK-HEP-1 and 293T
author_acknowledged_limitations: HFD duration/concentration 'insufficient to fully induce liver fibrosis'; field is early and mechanisms need more work; pure MP/NP cytotoxicity in human cells remains controversial; opposing effects on chow vs HFD may reflect basal metabolic status
independent_methodological_concerns: RNA-seq n never stated; DEGs called at UNCORRECTED p<0.05 with no DE tool named; no HFD vs CD contrast; dose is per animal (0.5 mg/day) while HFD mice end 25-37% heavier, so mg/kg diverges between diet arms; the abstract's 'no effects on chow' is contradicted by its own CD+PS-NPs macrophage, neutrophil, collagen and 361-DEG results; title claims impaired acidification but imaging shows the vacuoles ARE acidic
accessions_as_stated: NONE - no accession for a full liver transcriptome
verified_data_availability: 'All data ... included in this published article and its additional files'. No repository despite generating RNA-seq. DEG lists cannot be re-derived.
relevance_to_project: Closest design match WITH liver RNA-seq (2x2, male C57BL/6J, n=6). Instructive on both of the team's concerns: pairwise-only inference and uncorrected DE thresholds.

title: Developmental Environmental Chronotoxicity by Polystyrene Nanoplastics Exacerbates High-Fat Diet-Induced Pediatric MAFLD Through Circadian Disruption and Mitochondrial Dysfunction
authors: Xu P, Huang S, Zhu L, Huang J, Li K, Li G, Wu J, Zhou M, Zhou F, Ding Z, Shen Y
biological_question: Does developmental stage determine susceptibility to PS-NP exacerbation of HFD-induced MAFLD, via circadian and mitochondrial disruption?
experimental_design: Two age cohorts (juvenile 3 wk, adult 8 wk), each a 2x2: diet (chow vs HFD) x PS-NPs, 10 weeks; plus in-vivo AICAR/SR9009 rescue
species_strain_sex_age: Mouse, C57BL/6J, MALE; juvenile and adult cohorts
tissue: Liver; serum; HepG2 and Huh7 cells
biological_replicates_per_group: Phenotype n=6; RNA-seq n=5 (40 libraries across 8 groups); western n=5; in vitro n=3-6
particle_size: 100 nm nominal; MEASURED 115.4 +/- 1.5 nm, PDI 0.041, zeta -30.9 mV (Rigor Biotechnology FF3301G)
characterisation_and_endotoxin: BEST IN SET: DLS, PDI, zeta, SEM morphology, daily stability checks over the 3-day replacement cycle, and a labelled-vs-unlabelled comparison. Endotoxin still NOT reported
dose: 20 ug/mL in drinking water; estimated intake ~21.7-25.5 ug/g body weight/week
route_vehicle_duration: Oral, drinking water, replaced every 3 d, 10 wk
diet_metabolic_stress_model: Chow (unspecified) vs HFD D12492 (60 kcal% fat)
groups_and_controls: NC, PS, HFD, HFD+PS (HP) within each age cohort
data_types: Bulk liver RNA-seq (DNBSEQ-T7, PE150, median 43.78M clean reads, alignment rates reported, single batch); qPCR; western (BMAL1, p-AMPK); H&E with BLINDED NAS; Oil Red O; TEM; isolated-mitochondria JC-1 and CPT1 activity; ATP/ADP; Seahorse; GTT/ITT; serum biochemistry
statistical_computational_methods: DESeq2, |log2FC|>=1 and adjusted p<0.05, PAIRWISE contrasts; GO/KEGG with Bonferroni; phenotypes TWO-WAY ANOVA (HFD x PS-NPs) with Tukey
formal_interaction_tested: PARTIAL - phenotypes are modelled with a real two-way ANOVA including an interaction term, but no interaction F or p is printed for any in-vivo phenotype; transcriptomics has NO interaction model. Age is two separate 2x2s, not a three-way test
main_findings_and_directions: Juvenile-specific exacerbation: liver index, ALT, AST, LDL-C, HDL-C, TG, T-CHO, NAS and Oil Red O all higher in juvenile HFD+PS vs HFD; adults showed 'limited additional pathological changes'. Body weight, adiposity, GTT and ITT NOT further altered. p-AMPK progressively suppressed; ATP/ADP, membrane potential and CPT1 activity down; cristae density reduced. Lipogenic Fasn, Lxra, Srebp1c progressively UP; FAO/OXPHOS genes biphasic (up after single stressors, down after combined). BMAL1 protein down with single exposures but UP under co-exposure (non-monotonic). AICAR and SR9009 rescued in vitro and in vivo.
dir_lipid_lipogenesis: UP under combined exposure (Fasn, Lxra, Srebp1c)
dir_ppar_fao: PPARalpha NOT directly measured; FAO proxied by Cpt1a/Acadl/Pgc-1a mRNA and CPT1 activity - net DOWN under combined exposure
dir_cholesterol: Serum and hepatic total cholesterol UP; no synthesis genes
dir_inflammation: Essentially not studied (only the NAS sub-score)
dir_oxidative_stress: ROS up in cells only; NO in-vivo oxidative-stress measurement
dir_mitochondria: BEST-SUPPORTED THEME - cristae, membrane potential, ATP, CPT1 activity and respiration all down
dir_circadian: Core clock perturbed but NON-MONOTONIC at a single time point; rhythmicity assessed only in vitro after synchronisation
experimentally_validated: Extensive functional validation plus pharmacological rescue in vivo AND in vitro. NO genetic validation - authors state tissue-specific loss/gain-of-function 'will be essential'
author_acknowledged_limitations: Individual intake could not be quantified (group housing, drinking water); only one formulation/size/concentration; environmental relevance of the dose needs evaluation; circadian changes characterised at selected time points and in vitro; MALE ONLY; single-time-point clock measurement 'requires caution'; cell models lack systemic entrainment; transcriptional activation may be adaptive; CPT1 assay not isoform-specific; drug off-target effects possible
independent_methodological_concerns: Cage-level exposure and intake with the mouse declared the statistical unit; chow not matched to the purified HFD; interaction F/p never printed; no DEG counts anywhere in the main text; which 5 of 6 mice were sequenced is unstated; HFD shifts feeding rhythm, which could drive the clock-gene changes; a cell-culture figure legend names 'HFD x PS-NPs' as factors
accessions_as_stated: NONE - 40 RNA-seq libraries with no stated accession
verified_data_availability: 'available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request'. No repository. Not reusable.
relevance_to_project: THE methodological benchmark in this set: the only study that controls sampling time (all collections in a ZT4-ZT6 window) - the control the team's clock-phase confound lacks - and the only one with full particle characterisation and reported sequencing depth/alignment rates.

title: Low-Dose Polystyrene Nanoplastics Alleviate High-Fat Diet-Induced Hepatic Injury via AMPK/mTOR-Mediated Lipophagy Activation
authors: Luo G, He Z, Zhang Y, Liu B, Yang G, Liu W, Huang B, Wang Q, Li W, Chen L
journal: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver
biological_question: What are the hepatic effects of LOW-dose microplastics under a high-fat diet?
experimental_design: NOT VERIFIED (abstract only). Methods name two groups (HFD, HFD-NP) but Results mention an 'NP group', implying a 2x2
dose: 'Low-dose' - NO NUMERIC DOSE GIVEN (the key missing number)
data_types: H&E histology; hepatic lipid oxidation/utilisation; transcriptomics (platform NOT VERIFIED); primary hepatocyte assays
statistical_computational_methods: NOT VERIFIED - no test, threshold, DE tool or correction named in the abstract
formal_interaction_tested: NOT VERIFIED - claims are framed as pairwise group comparisons
main_findings_and_directions: CONTRASTING / PROTECTIVE: lipid accumulation, inflammation and fibrosis in HFD livers were 'greatly diminished in HFD-NP group, compared with HFD group'. PS-NPs alone caused 'no obvious pathological changes'. In vitro PS-NPs alleviated palmitic-acid-induced apoptosis and lipid droplets. Hepatic lipid oxidation and utilisation enhanced. Transcriptomics implicated AMPK activation and mTOR inhibition driving lipophagy.
dir_ppar_fao: PPARalpha not named; fatty-acid oxidation UP
experimentally_validated: Histology and cell assays per abstract; the causal step is autophagy inhibition in vitro
independent_methodological_concerns: ABSTRACT ONLY and the decisive number - the dose - is absent. Species differs (rat, not mouse). Group structure ambiguous. Cannot be used as evidence for a specific protective dose without the full text.
verified_data_availability: Unknown - subscription full text not obtained.
relevance_to_project: The direct counter-example to the exacerbation literature: same broad exposure, opposite direction, with AMPK/mTOR/lipophagy proposed - the inverse of the mTOR-up/autophagy-blocked mechanism in ijbs2025.

title: Polystyrene nanoplastics induce hepatic steatosis by disrupting autophagic degradation of NCoR1 and suppressing PPARα-mediated fatty acid oxidation
authors: Fang Y, Wei T, Zhang Z, Li Y, Yang M, Chen H, Wang Y, Hao R, Li Y, Sun Z, Wang J
biological_question: Do PS nanoplastics worsen HFD steatosis by blocking autophagic degradation of NCoR1 and suppressing PPARalpha-driven fatty-acid oxidation?
experimental_design: 2x2: diet (ND vs HFD) x PSNPs, 90 days. Omics run on only TWO of the four groups
species_strain_sex_age: Mouse, C57BL/6J, MALE, 5-6 wk at start
biological_replicates_per_group: Phenotype n=10; most assays n=6; RNA-seq n=4 (HFD and HFD+PSNP only); metabolomics n=6 (same two groups); mechanistic imaging/IP n=3; TEM n=2
polymer: Polystyrene (pristine for the 90-day study; red-fluorescent only for biodistribution)
particle_size: 50 nm nominal; MEASURED TEM 49.24 +/- 5.31 nm; DLS 53.35 nm, zeta -30.83 mV, PDI 0.05 (full table reported)
characterisation_and_endotoxin: Good: TEM sizing of 500 particles, DLS/zeta/PDI in water and medium at 0 and 24 h. Endotoxin NOT reported
dose: 150 mg/kg body weight/day (derived from the UPPER range of estimated human intake with a 12.3x conversion factor)
route_vehicle_duration: Oral gavage daily, 90 d, vehicle ddH2O (gavage matched across groups)
diet_metabolic_stress_model: ND (brand/composition NOT reported) vs HFD D12492 (60% kcal fat)
data_types: Bulk liver RNA-seq (NovaSeq 6000, 150 bp PE; DEPTH NOT REPORTED); untargeted metabolomics; RT-qPCR; western; immunoprecipitation; IHC/IF; H&E with NAS; Oil Red O; TEM; hepatic TG/TC/FFA/FC; hepatic (not serum) ALT/AST
statistical_computational_methods: DESeq2, adjusted p<0.05 and |log2FC|>1 -> 236 DEGs (95 up, 141 down); metabolomics VIP>1 plus adjusted p; phenotypes TWO-WAY ANOVA with Tukey
formal_interaction_tested: MODEL EXISTS but NO interaction F or p is reported; all printed significance is pairwise vs ND or vs HFD. Omics cannot test interaction at all (only 2 of 4 groups profiled)
main_findings_and_directions: No liver injury and NO inflammation or fibrosis (ALT/AST unchanged, NAS below NASH criteria, serum inflammatory factors and fibrosis staining unchanged). Steatosis worsened on HFD: hepatic TG highest in HFD+PSNP, TC and FFA unchanged. PSNPs alone produced NO hepatic phenotype. KEGG: PPAR signalling SUPPRESSED along with steroid and terpenoid backbone biosynthesis. Acsl3, Hmgcs1, Fabp4, Fabp5, Cyp4a31 down; Acsl3/Cpt1a/Acox1/Hmgcs1 down at mRNA and ACSL3/CPT1A/HMGCS1 at protein. Long-chain fatty acids and acylcarnitines accumulate. NCoR1 protein up; LC3B protein down with Lc3b mRNA unchanged; NCoR1 phosphorylation and nuclear translocation up; p-mTOR and p-S6 up. Rapamycin rescued in vitro.
dir_lipid_lipogenesis: Hepatic TG UP but de novo lipogenesis and uptake genes explicitly UNCHANGED - steatosis framed as a catabolic defect
dir_ppar_fao: SUPPRESSED - the key direction. Cpt1a, Acox1, Acsl3, Cyp4a31 DOWN. Authors state 'suppression (rather than activation) of this pathway'. Ppara itself never measured
dir_cholesterol: DOWN/suppressed (steroid and terpenoid biosynthesis; HMGCS1 protein down) while hepatic TC unchanged
dir_inflammation: NO CHANGE - treated as a design feature (clean 'first hit' model)
dir_mitochondria: Inferred only (no membrane potential, ATP or respirometry)
dir_circadian: NOT STUDIED - and mice were fasted overnight, which itself activates PPARalpha in every group
experimentally_validated: FAO suppression validated at mRNA and protein (n=6). The causal chain is correlative in vivo; the only causal experiment is rapamycin in L-02 cells, in a supplementary figure. NO genetic manipulation of any kind; NCoR1-PPARalpha interaction never measured (no co-IP, no ChIP)
author_acknowledged_limitations: Parallel pathways and the precise NCoR1 phosphorylation sites need mapping; the autophagic receptor recognising NCoR1 is unidentified; phospho-NCoR1 and S6K2-specific antibodies unavailable (workarounds used); species differences in PPARalpha biology
independent_methodological_concerns: Omics cover only 2 of 4 groups so no interaction is possible; RNA-seq depth, mapping rate and batch never reported; SEM stated in Methods but SD in every legend; ALT/AST measured in liver homogenate rather than serum; overnight fast pre-activates PPARalpha; mechanistic core runs on n=2-3; L-02 is widely flagged as HeLa-contaminated with no authentication statement; Hmgcs1 (cholesterol pathway) treated as an FAO target where Hmgcs2 is the PPARalpha ketogenic target; 'environmentally relevant' overstates an upper-range dose
accessions_as_stated: NONE - neither RNA-seq nor metabolomics deposited
verified_data_availability: 'All data are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request'. Not reusable.
relevance_to_project: The clearest PPARalpha direction conflict with Jung 2026 (suppressed vs induced), with every differing condition documented - polymer, size, route, dose, duration and an overnight fast.

title: Size-dependent plastic exposure disrupts macrophage function and tissue-specific metabolism
authors: Makdissi N, Viola MF, Steinheuer LM, Blank-Stein N, Kardinal R, Musacchio F, Franco Taveras E, Aliprandi V, Sieckmann K, Abdulkadyrov A, Mayer ML, Diefenbach-Wilke ML, Fink D, Beckert H, Böhmdorfer S, Deveuve Q, Graelmann FJ, Mauel K, Kronau N, Thomas J, Bejarano D, Schlitzer A, Högler S, Yaghmour MH, Heeren J, Thiele C, Kenner L, Meissner F, Nimmerjahn F, Fuhrmann M, Wachten D, Thurley K, Mass E
biological_question: Do ingested micro/nanoplastics accumulate in Kupffer cells and reprogram them in a size-dependent way, with downstream hepatocyte and systemic metabolic effects?
experimental_design: Chronic weekly gavage 12 wk (Ctrl, 50 nm NP, 500 nm MP) at 100/10/1 mg/kg; acute bioavailability; 6-month washout; a separate HFD arm; genetic fate-mapping and Kupffer-cell depletion
species_strain_sex_age: Mouse, C57BL/6JRcc, MALE 8-12 wk (both sexes only in one transgenic line; co-culture hepatocytes from female mice)
tissue: Liver (omics); spleen, BAT, gWAT, brain, blood, intestine and others by flow cytometry
biological_replicates_per_group: snRNA-seq n=2 per condition; lipidomics n=9/8/10; Oil Red O n=6/10/9; body weight n=35/32/39; functional assays n=6-12; proteomics n not reported (3 samples excluded)
polymer: Polystyrene, carboxylated (also gold-core PS-coated and europium variants)
particle_size: 50 nm and 500 nm for chronic work; 100 and 300 nm in the acute screen. Measured values in an unread supplementary figure
characterisation_and_endotoxin: DLS Z-average, PDI and zeta measured (values in Supplementary Fig. 1, not read). Endotoxin NOT reported. Authors could NOT quantify tissue plastic burden - europium signal lost and pyrolysis-GC-MS failed
dose: 100 mg/kg standard, with 10 and 1 mg/kg titration arms; gold-core arm 0.8 mg/week
route_vehicle_duration: Oral gavage ONCE WEEKLY, 12 wk, vehicle PBS
diet_metabolic_stress_model: Control diet 13 kJ% fat (Ssniff E15748-047); HFD 60 kJ% fat (Ssniff E15742-347) in a separate staged arm. Main experiments are chow-fed/lean; NO MASH diet
groups_and_controls: PBS control, NP (50 nm), MP (500 nm)
data_types: Single-NUCLEUS RNA-seq of liver (10x, ~30,000 reads/nucleus); liver shotgun lipidomics; DIA proteomics of isolated Kupffer cells; flow cytometry; confocal and electron microscopy; histology with blinded pathology; serum ALT/AST and Luminex; GTT/ITT; indirect calorimetry; qPCR
statistical_computational_methods: snRNA-seq DE by Wilcoxon with BH (thresholds differ between Methods and a figure legend); ORA via clusterProfiler; VIPER TF activity; CellChat; proteomics Welch's t-test with FDR<0.05; phenotypes ANOVA/Kruskal-Wallis with FDR; Grubbs' outlier removal
formal_interaction_tested: NO - the HFD 'exacerbation' is never tested as a particle x diet interaction
main_findings_and_directions: Kupffer cells are the dominant hepatic reservoir; hepatocytes contain no detectable particles. MP (not NP) increased hepatic neutral lipid at 12 wk (not 4 wk) and reduced glycogen at 100 and 10 mg/kg but not 1 mg/kg. NO hepatocellular injury or fibrosis (ALT/AST unchanged, Sirius Red negative). Lipidomics: MP increased LPC, LPE and sphingomyelin species. Hepatocytes had the most DEGs; de novo lipogenesis SUPPRESSED with fatty-acid uptake and lipoprotein receptors UP in both NP and MP. Apolipoproteins up in Kupffer cells, with APOC3 and TTR confirmed at protein level. KEY: Kupffer cells from MP mice co-cultured with naive hepatocytes were SUFFICIENT to induce hepatocyte lipid droplets. MP impaired Fc-gamma-receptor platelet clearance at 4 wk (before lipid accumulation) and E. coli clearance. NO inflammation (no cell-number or cytokine increases). Under HFD, MP increased and NP DECREASED hepatic lipid.
dir_lipid_lipogenesis: De novo lipogenesis SUPPRESSED, uptake UP (same direction as Jung 2026's lipogenic down-regulation)
dir_ppar_fao: PPARalpha appears only as a VIPER-predicted TF activity and 'no single transcription factor reached significance'
dir_cholesterol: 'Cholesterol homoeostasis' among enriched hepatocyte terms; bile-acid synthesis genes up
dir_inflammation: EXPLICITLY ABSENT - no myeloid expansion, no serum cytokine rise. Authors conclude reprogramming rather than classical inflammation
dir_oxidative_stress: Not measured (loss of MAFG/MAFK predicted only)
dir_circadian: Not addressed; sacrifice time not reported
experimentally_validated: STRONGEST FUNCTIONAL VALIDATION IN THE SET: ex-vivo co-culture sufficiency, in-vivo phagocytosis and bacterial-clearance assays, genetic fate-mapping and diphtheria-toxin Kupffer-cell depletion. The HIF-1alpha/apolipoprotein axis and all VIPER TF activities remain INFERRED
author_acknowledged_limitations: Could not quantify tissue plastic burden (europium and pyrolysis-GC-MS both failed); chow-fed lean model with no MASH diet; mediator of the co-culture effect not identified
independent_methodological_concerns: snRNA-seq n=2 per condition - very low for DEG claims; DE q-threshold differs between Methods (0.05) and a figure legend (0.1); gold-core dose stated inconsistently (0.8 mg/week vs 0.8 mg/kg twice weekly); no cage or batch covariate anywhere; male only; HFD arm staged (particles stopped 6 weeks before the end)
accessions_as_stated: GEO GSE291616 (liver snRNA-seq); PRIDE PXD072158 (Kupffer-cell proteomics); Metabolomics Workbench ST003776 (liver lipidomics); bonndata 10.60507/FK2/M42B8O (histology)
verified_data_availability: VERIFIED, the best-documented in the set: GSE291616 public (6 samples, 2 per group, 10x matrix files, SRA PRJNA1234520); PXD072158 public at PRIDE (mouse liver Kupffer cells); ST003776 public at Metabolomics Workbench (28 samples: 9 PBS, 9 50-nm, 10 500-nm); bonndata DOI resolves. No code repository.
relevance_to_project: Mechanistically the strongest paper found, and it shows an alternative route to a hepatocyte lipid phenotype - macrophage-mediated, with no particles inside hepatocytes and no inflammation. Directly relevant to interpreting bulk liver signal.

title: Chronic PET-Microplastic Exposure: Disruption of Gut-Liver Homeostasis and Risk of Hepatic Steatosis
authors: Park S, Kim MJ, Shin JH, Kim E, Son M, Lee S
biological_question: Does chronic exposure to environmentally mimetic PET microplastics disrupt the gut-liver axis and cause steatosis?
experimental_design: 2 groups (control vs PET-MP) at two time points (8 and 29 weeks). NOT a 2x2 - no diet factor
species_strain_sex_age: Mouse, C57BL/6N, MALE, 4-5 wk at start
biological_replicates_per_group: 8/8 at 8 wk and 9/8 at 29 wk (total 33); RNA-seq n=4 per group; liver weight 'n=21' and ALT 'n=13' unexplained; microbiome/histology/qPCR n not reported
polymer: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET), produced in-house by abrading drinking-water bottles - environmentally mimetic, irregular
particle_size: Sieved <500 um; laser diffraction: ~60% between 10-100 um and 26% between 100-200 um
characterisation_and_endotoxin: UNUSUALLY GOOD contamination control (triple rinse, ethanol, laminar flow, UV-C, cleaned steel mill, no autoclave) and FIB-SEM morphology. Endotoxin, zeta potential and leachates (antimony, phthalates) NOT reported
dose: 5 mg per week in feed (~170-200 mg/kg/week); derived from a human intake estimate scaled by body weight
diet_metabolic_stress_model: Standard chow only for both groups; NO dietary challenge, so no MP x diet interaction exists in this paper
groups_and_controls: Control (did not ingest PET-MP) vs MP; no vehicle or inert-particle control
data_types: Bulk liver RNA-seq (MGI DNBSEQ G400-RS; DEPTH NOT REPORTED); 16S rRNA; histology (H&E with blinded NAS, Oil Red O, Masson, PAS); IHC (a-SMA, PLIN2); IF (CD68); qRT-PCR (Tnfa, Il6); serum ALT; DXA; pyrolysis-GC/MS of liver
statistical_computational_methods: Unpaired t-tests at each time point; NO two-way ANOVA, no exposure x time interaction, no multiplicity correction. RNA-seq DE TOOL, THRESHOLDS AND CORRECTION NOT REPORTED AT ALL
formal_interaction_tested: Not applicable (no diet factor); even exposure x time was never tested
main_findings_and_directions: Body weight and fat mass up at 29 wk (not 8 wk). Microbiota separated by exposure at both time points (Adonis R2 0.176 p=0.006 and 0.114 p=0.028); Firmicutes up, Bacteroidota down; intestinal mucus reduced. Liver: NAFLD-like histology with higher NAS, serum ALT up, CD68+ macrophages up, Tnfa and Il6 up, Oil Red O and PLIN2 up, early fibrosis (a-SMA, Masson, collagen genes) at 29 wk only. DEGs small: 13 down/15 up at 8 wk; 24 down/59 up at 29 wk. PET was NOT detected in liver by pyrolysis-GC/MS.
dir_lipid_lipogenesis: Lipid-droplet genes UP (Plin2, Chka, Ces1c); PLIN2 protein confirmed
dir_ppar_fao: NOT reported in this study's own data (PPAR appears only as cited literature)
dir_cholesterol: 'Steroid metabolism' enriched (omics only); no serum lipid panel
dir_inflammation: UP (Tnfa, Il6 by qPCR; CD68 by IF; lobular inflammation in NAS)
dir_mitochondria: Abstract claims mitochondrial gene downregulation but no supporting panel was locatable in the main text; no functional assay
dir_fibrosis: UP at 29 weeks (a-SMA, Masson, collagen transcripts); absent at 8 weeks
experimentally_validated: Inflammation (qPCR, IF), lipid (ORO, PLIN2 IHC) and fibrosis (histology, IHC) validated. DEG-level claims are omics-only and not reproducible from the reported methods
author_acknowledged_limitations: Definitive evidence of direct particle accumulation in liver remains to be established; oxidative stress, circulating LPS and ferroptosis markers deferred to future studies
independent_methodological_concerns: ABSTRACT CONTRADICTS RESULTS: abstract claims 'hepatomegaly' while Results state 'no statistically significant differences' in liver weight; abstract claims bile-acid disruption but no bile acid was measured (only faecal colour); DE tool, fold-change cut-off, FDR threshold and read depth are nowhere stated so the DEG counts cannot be reproduced; n for several panels unexplained (21, 13); route stated inconsistently; final age inconsistent (34 vs 33 weeks); no data accession at all
verified_data_availability: 'available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request'. Neither RNA-seq nor 16S deposited. Not reusable.
relevance_to_project: Only PET in-vivo study in the set and the only one using environmentally mimetic abraded particles. Shows a liver phenotype WITHOUT demonstrated hepatic particle burden - supporting indirect, gut-mediated mechanisms.

title: Integrated computational analysis identifies FABP4, PTGS2, and HPGD as Key molecular targets linking PET microplastic exposure to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease
authors: Zhang Y, Yu Y, Ge B, Gong D, Zheng L, Wang Y, Chen P
biological_question: Which predicted PET protein targets overlap with MASLD-associated genes in public human liver data?
experimental_design: ENTIRELY IN SILICO - no exposure, no animals, no wet lab
biological_replicates_per_group: 38 control and 58 NAFLD samples pooled across three GEO cohorts; per-cohort breakdown not restated
polymer: PET modelled ONLY as a small-molecule SMILES, NOT as a particle
particle_size: Not applicable - no particle is modelled
dose: Not applicable - no exposure or dose-response
diet_metabolic_stress_model: Not applicable; the disease axis is human MASLD vs control
data_types: Public human liver expression data; chemical target prediction (ChEMBL, PharmMapper, SwissTargetPrediction); STRING PPI; CIBERSORT; AutoDock Vina docking; 100 ns GROMACS molecular dynamics; CTD comparison
statistical_computational_methods: Quantile normalisation + ComBat; limma (Methods threshold |log2FC|>=1.5 with BH FDR<0.05); WGCNA; cytoHubba/MCODE; docking energy cut-off -5.0 kcal/mol. NO machine-learning classifier, no cross-validation, no ROC/AUC
main_findings_and_directions: 229 predicted PET targets; 19 overlapping with MASLD genes; hub genes FABP4, PTGS2, HPGD; CIBERSORT shows M2 macrophages and gd T cells up with monocytes, dendritic cells and naive B cells down in MASLD; docking -6.3 to -6.9 kcal/mol; complexes stable over 100 ns
dir_lipid_lipogenesis: Implicated via FABP4 and lipid-metabolism enrichment - PREDICTION only
dir_inflammation: Implicated via PTGS2 and HPGD, but the immune shifts are MASLD-associated, not PET-induced
experimentally_validated: NONE - no qPCR, western, cell or animal validation anywhere. Every finding is COMPUTATIONAL-PREDICTION
author_acknowledged_limitations: Analyses relied on computational prediction and public data 'which require experimental validation in cell culture and animal models'; docking and dynamics 'do not account for the complex in vivo environment'
independent_methodological_concerns: PET is modelled as a monomer-like soluble fragment, so the Discussion's leap to particles accumulating in hepatocytes is unsupported; DEG thresholds and counts are internally inconsistent (Methods |log2FC|>=1.5 with FDR; Results |log2FC|>=2 with raw p giving 357; elsewhere 265); force field stated as CHARMM36 in one section and AMBER99SB-ILDN in the next; 'six algorithms' listed as seven; cohorts described as microarray in the abstract but 'bulk RNA-seq' in the deconvolution methods
accessions_as_stated: GEO GSE37031, GSE63067, GSE89632; GitHub pipipeng288/Code; Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.18925269
verified_data_availability: VERIFIED: all three GEO series public (15, 18 and 63 samples respectively); GitHub repo exists (5 folders, created 2026-03-09) and the Zenodo archive resolves to record 18925270 with a 29 KB code zip. Inputs and code are genuinely reusable even though the biology is unvalidated.
relevance_to_project: A cautionary comparator for the 'network toxicology' genre the team could be tempted to imitate: named hub genes with no exposure data and no validation.

title: Microplastics detected in cirrhotic liver tissue
authors: Horvatits T, Tamminga M, Liu B, Sebode M, Carambia A, Fischer L, Püschel K, Huber S, Fischer EK
biological_question: Do microplastics accumulate in human liver, and does cirrhosis favour it?
experimental_design: Proof-of-concept case series: 6 patients with cirrhosis and 5 individuals without liver disease; 17 tissue samples
biological_replicates_per_group: 6 cirrhotic, 5 non-cirrhotic individuals; small per-organ n
polymer: Six different polymers detected (which six NOT VERIFIED here; abbreviations defined include PS, PET, PVC, PMMA, POM, PP)
characterisation_and_endotoxin: Procedural blanks processed identically; LOD = mean + 3 SD, LOQ = mean + 10 SD; Raman confirmation of polymer identity
dose: Not applicable - environmental human exposure, unquantified
groups_and_controls: Cirrhotic vs non-cirrhotic tissue vs procedural blanks
data_types: Chemical digestion, Nile red staining, fluorescence microscopy, Raman spectroscopy. NO molecular profiling of any kind
statistical_computational_methods: Kruskal-Wallis with Dunn post hoc; Wilcoxon for within-patient organ comparisons
main_findings_and_directions: MP concentrations in cirrhotic liver significantly higher than procedural blanks (n=6, p=0.009). All liver, kidney and spleen samples from individuals without liver disease tested negative at the stated limit of detection. Six polymers, 4-30 um.
experimentally_validated: Analytical detection with Raman confirmation and procedural blanks. NO causal or mechanistic claim is made
author_acknowledged_limitations: Digestion prevents localisation (cell type unknown); 4 um detection floor; 'the sample size was rather small'; no dietary or lifestyle data; 'Adjustment for potential confounders, such as age or sex was not possible'; no unified methodology across labs; findings need reproducing in larger cohorts
independent_methodological_concerns: The primary comparison is cirrhotic liver vs procedural blanks rather than cirrhotic vs non-cirrhotic liver; reverse causation is explicitly open (portal hypertension may increase translocation); whether polyethylene was among the six polymers should be checked before citing this to support a PE-specific rationale
verified_data_availability: 'Data are available on request from the authors'. Not reusable.
relevance_to_project: Human-relevance anchor only: particles detectable in diseased but not healthy liver, no exposure quantification, no molecular data.
